```{r}
checks <- read.csv("validation/validation_checks.csv")
missing <- read.csv("validation/missingness.csv")
timings <- read.csv("validation/runtime.csv")
main <- read.csv("../data/processed/final_data.csv", fileEncoding = "UTF-8")
agent <- read.csv("../data/processed/final_data_agent.csv", fileEncoding = "UTF-8")
stopifnot(all(checks$passed), identical(main, agent))
```

## What was compared

The two Week 3 implementations were rerun from the unchanged raw files in
separate `Rscript --vanilla` processes. The primary script uses `dplyr` and
`tidyr`; the comparison script uses base R reshaping, aggregation, and merging.
Each script reads the raw inputs and writes its own output file. Their exported
CSVs are then compared, including column order, types, values, and missingness.

Both implementations were prepared with coding-agent assistance in Week 3.
This is a comparison between two implementations of the same specification.
It does not establish an independent human-versus-agent validation or prove
that the supplied study definition is correct.

## Results

Each dataset contains **`r nrow(main)` country-years and `r ncol(main)` variables**.
All **`r nrow(main) * ncol(main)` cells** and their missing-value positions match.
The regenerated files also match the archived Week 3 files exactly. There are
no output discrepancies requiring a correction to the final data.

```{r}
knitr::kable(data.frame(
  Item = c("Countries", "Outcome years", "Country-year rows", "Duplicate keys",
           "Prior-year conflict = 1", "Earthquake = 1", "Drought = 1"),
  Result = c(length(unique(main$iso)), "2000-2019", nrow(main),
    anyDuplicated(main[c("iso", "year")]), sum(main$armed_conflict_lag1),
    sum(main$earthquake), sum(main$drought))))
```

The `r nrow(checks)` checks include raw mortality and covariate values, unique
keys, one-year lag endpoints, and deliberately chosen edge cases. A 25-death
conflict qualifies; separate conflicts with 12 and 13 deaths do not jointly
qualify under the selected rule. Missing values on real conflict events cause
an error rather than becoming zero.

```{r}
knitr::kable(checks, col.names = c("Check", "Passed"))
```

## Decisions retained after review

Conflict deaths are summed within country, source year, and conflict ID. A
country-year is exposed if at least one conflict has 25 or more deaths, then
that flag is assigned to the following outcome year. For example, 2000 outcomes
use 1999 conflict exposure. All supplied source years are present. Pooling
unrelated conflict IDs before applying the threshold would change 13 exposure
values, as recorded in
[conflict_definition_differences.csv](validation/conflict_definition_differences.csv).
That alternative is a definition change, not a disagreement between these scripts.

Missing outcomes and covariates are preserved. No country is dropped because
of missing measures. No-event conflict placeholders have both the conflict ID
and deaths missing; they are distinct from incomplete event records. Repeated
rows in the reduced conflict extract are retained because a unique event
identifier is absent.

```{r}
knitr::kable(missing[missing$missing_n > 0, ],
  col.names = c("Variable", "Missing rows", "Missing (%)"), digits = 2)
```

The panel includes all 186 countries supplied for class. It does not impose the
published paper's final sample exclusions. Covariate units remain as supplied;
the raw CSV does not provide a complete measurement codebook.

## Reproducibility and next step

The validation runs succeeded in clean R sessions. The scripts use paths within
`week5`, declare the needed packages, and do not require downloaded data during
execution. Input checksums and the R session details are in `validation/`.

```{r}
knitr::kable(timings, col.names = c("Implementation", "Elapsed seconds"), digits = 3)
```

These one-run timings include R startup and package loading. They are not a
controlled performance comparison. Both implementations are practical for the
course data. The primary script remains the source for EDA because its named
steps are easier to follow. No data corrections were made after comparison.

From the repository root:

```sh
Rscript --vanilla week5/R/validate_data.R
Rscript --vanilla week5/R/summarise_eda.R
```

The exploratory results are in [eda.html](eda.html).
